verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly lists a first-party 'Code references' feature. Independent users corroborate that it answers where a flag is used in code, and that evaluation analytics surface unused flags, flags only ever served the default, and stale temporary flags. However, the first-party evidence is only a feature title, so the depth of stale-flag detection and the removal workflow is unproven. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of stale/unused flag detection, documented code-reference scanning setup (e.g., CI integration), and an evidenced cleanup/removal workflow for temporary flags.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can find stale flags and code references so temporary flags actually get removed from the codebase

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly even has a product feature that does this, called 'Code References.'
surfaces unused flags, flags only ever evaluated to the default, and flags only ever evaluated to one outcome
its analytics for spotting stale flags and marking temporary vs permanent ones to reduce tech debt
